source.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Efficiently Selects Flatter Minima Late in Training
source.authors: Zhan-Peng Zhou; Mingze Wang; Yuan Mao; Bing-Rui Li; Jun-Chi Yan

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies late-phase SAM and its effects on test performance and Hessian sharpness, but does not test the claim versions: it does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, the specified architecture comparisons, adaptive optimizers, large-batch effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper's rows concern its own late-phase optimizer-switching experiments and the test-performance/sharpness outcomes it reports. The adversarial-training robustness result is outside the claim's in-distribution generalization scope. Cited prior-work results are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study tests optimizer timing and its effects on test performance and Hessian sharpness, but none of V1–V8. In particular, it does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or rank training–test gaps against competing measures. Its AdamW-to-SAM experiment also lacks V4's adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find that late-phase SAM efficiently selects flatter minima with test performance comparable to full SAM, provide a two-phase theoretical explanation under simplifying assumptions, and conjecture that the final optimizer strongly shapes solution properties. Their theory does not explain early-phase SAM.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies switching between SGD and SAM, including late-phase application; the claim versions concern other interventions and comparisons. It uses CIFAR image classifiers and reports test performance and Hessian sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured outcomes vary with when SAM is applied: late-phase SAM yields test performance comparable to full SAM, while switching from SAM to SGD leaves a substantial gap at a SAM proportion of 0.8. The authors also report a perturbation-radius dependence for full SAM but no significant differences after switching to SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: A few final epochs of SAM after SGD yield test performance and Hessian spectral-norm sharpness comparable to full SAM; ending with SGD retains larger performance differences in the reported WideResNet settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The timing of SAM affects final test performance and unscaled Hessian sharpness, with late application sufficient to recover much of full SAM's benefit in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Test performance has negligible reported dependence on the earlier SAM radius after switching to SGD, whereas larger radii improve performance under full SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The influence of SAM perturbation radius on final test performance depends on the optimizer used at the end of training.

record.problems: The empirical comparisons report test-performance differences from full SAM rather than the training-test error gap in the claim. The paper's sharpness measure is the Hessian spectral norm, not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance. Several outcomes are described qualitatively, with precise values available only in figures. The theoretical analysis uses simplifying assumptions, including constant perturbation radius and squared loss.
record.rows_left_out: Adversarial-training robust and natural error outcomes in Section 5 and Figure 6 were left out because the reported robustness result concerns adversarial examples, outside the claim's in-distribution generalization scope. Figure-only curves without textual descriptions of specific values were not transcribed as numeric rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive methods versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including the specified recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions; this does not dispute the reported SAM effects. ASAM experiments still measure unscaled Hessian sharpness. Layer-normalized directions in Figure 14 visualize test-loss geometry rather than measuring V7's perturbation tolerance or training–test-gap ranking.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the stated tuning and regularization conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout’s effect on held-out error and its interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Removing the most memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: WideResNet-16-8 trained with SGD then SAM
rows.operation_detail: Switched from SGD to SAM for the final 1–5 epochs, then compared with full SAM training.
rows.measure: Test error and test loss relative to full SAM training.
rows.baseline: Full SAM training under the same settings; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Test error and loss comparable to full SAM training.
rows.note: The text reports this result explicitly; it does not give numeric test-error or test-loss values.
rows.check: The reported comparability with full SAM is supported by Section 3, but it measures no listed version. Test error and test loss should be separate rows.

rows.subject: WideResNet-16-8 trained with SGD then SAM
rows.operation_detail: Switched from SGD to SAM late in training and measured final solution sharpness.
rows.measure: Final solution sharpness, measured as the spectral norm of the Hessian.
rows.baseline: Full SAM training; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Sharpness drops once the SAM training proportion is greater than zero; last-few-epochs SAM is described as as effective as full SAM at finding flatter minima.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 reports means over three trials and standard-deviation error bars.
rows.note: This is Hessian spectral-norm sharpness, not magnitude-aware sharpness or a direct training-test gap measure.
rows.check: The reported Hessian spectral-norm decrease is supported, but this is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.

rows.subject: Switching from SGD to SAM across tested datasets and architectures
rows.size_stated: WideResNet, ResNet, and VGG configurations are described; individual sizes vary
rows.operation_detail: Switched from SGD to SAM at varying points while holding total training epochs fixed.
rows.measure: Test-loss and test-error differences from full SAM training.
rows.baseline: Full SAM training; exact values not stated.
rows.value: The generalization gap becomes negligible once SAM training proportion exceeds zero; the text says this trend is consistent across datasets and architectures.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 reports means over three trials and standard-deviation error bars; the text does not state uncertainty for the across-settings summary.
rows.note: Aggregate textual summary across settings; the source does not enumerate separate numerical outcomes for each setting here.
rows.check: The result concerns test-performance differences between training strategies, not training–test gaps. It aggregates architectures, datasets, and two measures that should be recorded separately.

rows.subject: Models trained with SAM then SGD
rows.size_stated: WideResNet-16-8 and WideResNet-28-10 are shown; further architectures in Appendix B.5
rows.operation_detail: Switched from SAM to SGD at varying points while holding total training epochs fixed.
rows.measure: Test-loss and test-error gaps from full SAM training.
rows.baseline: Full SAM training; exact values not stated.
rows.value: The gap remains substantial at SAM proportion 0.8; only full SAM training consistently finds the flat minima.
rows.uncertainty: Figures report means over three trials for Figure 5 and five trials for Figure 12, with standard-deviation error bars.
rows.note: The text reports test-performance gaps and sharpness trends together but gives no numeric values; its explicit 'only full SAM' statement concerns flat minima.
rows.check: The substantial gap at SAM proportion 0.8 is stated for Figure 5's WideResNets. Appendix B.5 instead describes ResNet-20 and VGG-16 gaps as substantial until the proportion exceeds 0.6. Separate these settings and separate test performance from sharpness; the full-SAM-only statement concerns flat minima.

rows.subject: Models trained with SAM then SGD
rows.operation_detail: Varied SAM perturbation radius before switching to SGD.
rows.baseline: Other tested perturbation-radius settings; exact values not stated.
rows.value: No significant differences across ρ values except at full SAM training, where a larger perturbation radius leads to better generalization.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 15 reports means over five trials with standard-deviation error bars; no significance test is stated.
rows.note: The text describes the result but gives no numeric values; 'no significant differences' is the authors' wording.
rows.check: The qualitative finding is supported but measures no listed version. Separate the negligible radius dependence after switching to SGD from the improvement with larger radius under full SAM, and separate test loss from test error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
